_meta.purpose: What every hostile DOES — its own tactics, not the bot's counters. Read monster_tactics_registry.js before using this.
_meta.difficulty_basis: normal — melee damage is typically x1.5 on hard and x0.5 on easy; several effects (cave spider poison, husk hunger) do not apply on easy at all

CONFIDENCE.warning: This document is AUTHORED FROM KNOWLEDGE, NOT MEASURED IN-WORLD. Nothing here has been observed by this fleet. Treat every field as a CLAIM to verify (Law 23), never as a sensed fact — a counter built on a wrong number will fail in a way that looks like bad tactics rather than bad data.
CONFIDENCE.verify_first: approach.speed_relative decides whether the bot can disengage on foot at all. It is the lowest-confidence field with the highest consequence — measure it before any counter relies on outrunning something.

VOCABULARY.note: Closed enums, so the interpreter reads a contract and not free text (Law 10). `group` is the TACTICAL taxonomy: two monsters share a group only if the SAME counter, unmodified, works on both. It replaced a descriptive `archetype` field on 2026-07-30 — two taxonomies over the same 42 monsters was a redundant route that would have drifted (Law 16). The RUNTIME authority is the table in combat_utils.js; this field is the design-time record and monster_tactics_test asserts the two agree.

FIELD_NOTES.aggro.range: blocks at which it will BEGIN pursuing, not the range at which it can attack
FIELD_NOTES.attack.range: 0 for melee-only; for projectile users this is effective firing range
FIELD_NOTES.approach.preferred_range: the gap it TRIES to hold. 0 = wants to be in your face; >0 = it will back off if the bot closes inside this
FIELD_NOTES.exploitable: mechanical openings the monster's own behaviour creates. Still facts about the MONSTER — the bot's counter for each is a separate layer and is deliberately not in this file
FIELD_NOTES.unverified: per-monster list of claims I am least sure of, so review lands there first
